Describes 18 consonants, 4 vowels, no phonological diphthongs, (N)(C)V(C) syllable, long vowels analysed as bisyllabic, NWS passage with phonemic and phonetic transcription (intonation arrows only, no stress marks). The words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur. Speaker from Batang Mitus, Tutong District.

sources.note: Sec. '3) Dusun' pp.155-156: Dusun proper (Kuala Ungur) and Bisaya? (Bebuloh) are mutually intelligible dialects (82% cognate); only phonetic remark is r = [r] coastal vs velar fricative inland. Swadesh lists carry no stress marks. Silent on stress.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert (researcher/depositor). RB2-003-A, field notebook, Sarawak 1971; notebook pp.31-40 'Bisaya (Limbang dialect)', speaker Sylvester Sarnagi of Ukong, dated Oct. 25 and 29. Kaipuleohone, University of Hawai'i Digital Language Archive, hdl:10125/33159 (deposited 2014).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Primary data, no prose statement. In the c. 200-item Limbang Bisaya wordlist every stress tick on a polysyllable stands before the FINAL syllable (du'o, ta'lu, a'pat, li'mo, u'nem, tu'ghu?, ba'lu?, mu'ped, a'buk, i'pen, di'le?, gi'ghak, ma'to, ku'ku?, ta'li, ba'ju?, a'su, a'puy, bin'tang, a'ku, i'kaw, temba'daw..); no penult ticks seen. Control: the Long Anap Kenyah list in the same notebook (pp.41-43) has many penult ticks, so the tick is a per-word record. Implicit evidence for final stress in citation forms only.
